Article 18
The family, in efforts to protect women's rights, has the role to:
a. protect women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations against women's rights in the household.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Coastal Regency
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Coastal.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of South Coastal Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit of the South Coastal Regency Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and increase of women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and in the state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Focal Point for Gender Mainstreaming is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is action that must be immediately taken to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is temporary housing used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
28. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

Article 28
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (3) What is meant by women crisis centre is an integrated service center initiated by the community spread throughout the regions, where the majority of services are provided for women and children victims of violence such as domestic violence, sexual violence and violence against children.

Article 26
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to complaint services submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 25 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of violence against women and children obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 23
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (3) Letter a Sufficiently clear.
Letter b Sufficiently clear.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d Sufficiently clear.
Letter e What is meant by assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health services, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence.

CHAPTER VII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 67
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Regional Government guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards, by facilitating the formulation of policies and regulations that serve as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection.
b. technical guidance and training, including:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement regarding the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists, and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each OPD for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. Provision of facilities: the Regional Government provides facilities, means, and infrastructure in implementing women’s empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the formation of nagari that care for women and children;
e. Provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) Supervision conducted by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. Monitoring, in the form of:
1. OPD leaders, in accordance with their duties and functions, are obligated to submit reports on the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection programs to the Regent.
2. Reports as referred to are submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
b. Evaluation, conducted in the form of:
1. The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
2. In conducting supervision and evaluation, the Regent may appoint an OPD in accordance with its duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation constitute evaluation material for policies of women’s empowerment and child protection programs.
(4) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), in order to realize the objectives of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection, shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 30
(1) Regional Government may provide safe houses for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.
(2) The provision of safe house services aims to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require a safe house include:
 a. their life is threatened;
 b. receiving rejection from family or community;
 c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
 d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 32
(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter f constitute actions by law enforcement apparatus to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil issues concerning women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
(3) Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
 a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
 b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
 c. legal assistance in the examination process at court;
 d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
 e. legal assistance in the mediation process.
(4) The Regional Government shall provide legal assistance to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil issues based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(5) In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Article 52
(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
(2) Every Child has the right to obtain Protection in educational units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, educational personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 51
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
(3) In the event that a Child victim of acts of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence shall be provided formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the educational unit and coordinated with UPTD PPA.

Letter e What is meant by the best interests of women and children is that in all actions concerning women and children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of women and children must be the primary consideration.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Part One
General

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESISIR SELATAN REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
I. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so forth.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, trafficking and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 Year 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 year 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing national and state life.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of the rights of women and children has been regulated in laws and regulations at the national level, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as improving the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Article 27
Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by the promotive aspect is to improve so that health status becomes increasingly improved, for example the provision of early breastfeeding initiation (IMD) and exclusive breastfeeding which can help increase immunity to disease because of colostrum and nutrients contained in breast milk, so that children are not easily affected by disease.
Letter b What is meant by the preventive aspect is to prevent from contracting disease or to keep healthy people to remain healthy, for example washing hands before eating and after defecating will prevent the occurrence of diarrheal disease.
Letter c What is meant by the curative aspect is the process of curing a person from a state of physical and psychological illness.
Letter d What is meant by the rehabilitative aspect is the process of maintaining so that a person who has recovered (not yet 100% recovered) returns to being fit as before.
Paragraph (2) What is meant by health rehabilitation carried out comprehensively is health rehabilitation carried out in a promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative manner and able to respond.
Paragraph (3) Letter a What is meant by medical services is services provided to reduce impact and prevent further injury, suffering and cost threats. includes:
1. physical examination and treatment of physical injuries;
2. treatment of psychological disorders;
3. treatment for prevention of sexually transmitted diseases;
4. treatment for prevention of HIV; and
5. reproductive health services.
Letter b What is meant by medicolegal services is services concerning management of various aspects related to medical services for legal purposes, for example collection of evidence from victims and preparation of VeR, includes:
1. visum et repertum (VeR) and psychological et repertum;
2. doctor's certificate; or
3. medical records.
What is meant by Visum et Repertum is a statement made by a doctor at the request of an authorized investigator regarding the results of medical examination of humans, whether alive or dead or parts or suspected parts of the human body, based on their scientific knowledge and under oath, for the purposes of justice.
Letter c What is meant by Psychosocial counseling is services by conducting counseling/handling of psychological trauma, providing assistance during the victim handling process, coordinating patient referrals and evaluating the completeness of victim case record documents, includes:
1. assistance from psychologists or social workers during the victim handling process; and
2. counseling/handling of psychological trauma.

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
I. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so forth.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, trafficking and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 Year 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 year 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing national and state life.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of the rights of women and children has been regulated in laws and regulations at the national level, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as improving the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

CONCERNING

I. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so forth.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, trafficking and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 Year 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 year 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing national and state life.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of the rights of women and children has been regulated in laws and regulations at the national level, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as improving the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Coastal Regency

3. Regent is the Regent of South Coastal.

5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit of the South Coastal Regency Regional Government.

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and in the state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Focal Point for Gender Mainstreaming is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is action that must be immediately taken to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is temporary housing used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Article 67

3. The results of supervision and evaluation constitute evaluation material for policies of women’s empowerment and child protection programs.

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and in the state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Focal Point for Gender Mainstreaming is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.

22. Safe House is temporary housing used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
28. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESISIR SELATAN REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
I. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so forth.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, trafficking and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 Year 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 year 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing national and state life.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of the rights of women and children has been regulated in laws and regulations at the national level, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as improving the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
I. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so forth.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, trafficking and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 Year 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 year 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing national and state life.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of the rights of women and children has been regulated in laws and regulations at the national level, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as improving the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Article 44
(1) In order to prepare planning, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation, as well as policy-making for development that is gender responsive and child-oriented, regional governments shall organize a gender and child data system.
(2) To organize the gender and child data system, accurate and accountable disaggregated data is required.

CHAPTER VII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 67

1. OPD leaders, in accordance with their duties and functions, are obligated to submit reports on the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection programs to the Regent.
2. Reports as referred to are submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

(1) In order to prepare planning, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation, as well as policy-making for development that is gender responsive and child-oriented, regional governments shall organize a gender and child data system.

Article 44
Paragraph (1) The gender and child data system is the institutionalization of the administration of gender and child affairs, consisting of components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in the region in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of the results of gender-responsive and child-sensitive development policies/programs/activities.

Article 24
(1) The implementation of UPTD PPA services shall be integrative in nature, either in the form of one-stop services or networked services, to provide optimal services to women and children experiencing problems.

(3) In the event that the implementation of integrated services is conducted through networking, UPTD PPA shall be responsible for the entire service referral process needed by women and children experiencing problems.
(4) Every element within the UPTD PPA environment, in carrying out its duties, must apply the principles of coordination, integration, synchronization, accountability, and transparency, both within the UPTD PPA environment and in relations among OPDs, relevant agencies, and elements of society.

Article 26
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to complaint services submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 25 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of violence against women and children obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 32
(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter f constitute actions by law enforcement apparatus to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil issues concerning women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
(3) Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
 a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
 b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
 c. legal assistance in the examination process at court;
 d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
 e. legal assistance in the mediation process.
(4) The Regional Government shall provide legal assistance to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil issues based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(5) In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Letter b What is meant by Psychologist is a personnel who has the capability to carry out psychological recovery for women and children victims of violence.

Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear.

Article 30
(1) Regional Government may provide safe houses for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.
(2) The provision of safe house services aims to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require a safe house include:
 a. their life is threatened;
 b. receiving rejection from family or community;
 c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
 d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 28
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter c is intended to restore and develop the capacity of women and children who experience social dysfunction due to criminal and/or civil matters to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:
a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) In the provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the UPTD PPA may cooperate with women crisis centres and/or existing social community organizations in the social sector.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESISIR SELATAN REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
I. GENERAL
Children are a trust as well as a gift from God Almighty, which we must always protect because inherent in them are dignity, honor, and rights as human beings that must be upheld. Children's human rights are part of human rights contained in the 1945 Constitution and the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child. From the perspective of national and state life, children are the future of the nation and the next generation of the nation's ideals, so that every child has the right to survival, growth, and development, to participate and has the right to protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as civil rights and freedoms.

Likewise with women, from women are expected to be born healthy, strong, resilient, noble, potential and quality children. Through the role of women in the family, society and the state will be born resilient generations who will continue the ideals of the nation.

As citizens of Indonesia, women also have the right to improve quality and develop themselves in accordance with their abilities, dignity and honor.

As assets and hope of the nation and state, children need to be given protection and safeguarded from all forms of acts of violence that will hinder their growth and development. Likewise with women, women need to be protected from acts of discrimination and acts of violence whether physical, psychological, mental, sexual and neglect. Because of their physical weakness compared to men and adults and because of the nature of women themselves, women and children often become objects of venting desires, anger, economic exploitation, violence (physical, psychological and sexual), cruelty, neglect, and so forth.

To realize the protection of women and children, support from laws and regulations is needed that can guarantee its implementation.

The Child Rights Convention affirms that preventive efforts must be made so that children are protected from kidnapping, trafficking and sale. In following up on the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Government established Law Number 23 Year 2002 as amended by Law Number 17 year 2016 concerning Child Protection.

Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights has included the rights of children, the implementation of obligations and responsibilities of parents, families, communities, government, and the state. Child protection in all its aspects is part of national development activities, particularly in advancing national and state life.

Parents, families, and communities are responsible for safeguarding and maintaining these human rights in accordance with the obligations imposed by law. Likewise in the context of implementing child protection, the State, Government and Regional Government are responsible for providing facilities and accessibility for children, especially in ensuring their growth and development optimally and in a directed manner.

That in order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family, community, national, and state life, it is deemed necessary to implement a gender mainstreaming strategy into the entire national development process, because it is an inseparable part of the functional activities of all organizations and institutions in the Region, for this it is necessary to encourage, make effective, and optimize gender mainstreaming efforts in an integrated and coordinated manner.

Although the protection of the rights of women and children has been regulated in laws and regulations at the national level, because the fulfillment of the constitutional rights of women and children as well as improving the quality of life of women and children is one of the mandatory affairs that is the duty, authority and responsibility of the Regional Government, in providing protection to women and children, the Pesisir Selatan Regency Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Coastal Regency
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Coastal.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of South Coastal Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit of the South Coastal Regency Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and increase of women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and in the state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Focal Point for Gender Mainstreaming is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is action that must be immediately taken to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is temporary housing used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
28. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

Article 30

Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by the promotive aspect is to improve so that health status becomes increasingly improved, for example the provision of early breastfeeding initiation (IMD) and exclusive breastfeeding which can help increase immunity to disease because of colostrum and nutrients contained in breast milk, so that children are not easily affected by disease.

Article 67
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Regional Government guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards, by facilitating the formulation of policies and regulations that serve as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection.

1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement regarding the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists, and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each OPD for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. Provision of facilities: the Regional Government provides facilities, means, and infrastructure in implementing women’s empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the formation of nagari that care for women and children;
e. Provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.

a. Monitoring, in the form of:
1. OPD leaders, in accordance with their duties and functions, are obligated to submit reports on the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection programs to the Regent.
2. Reports as referred to are submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

3. The results of supervision and evaluation constitute evaluation material for policies of women’s empowerment and child protection programs.
(4) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), in order to realize the objectives of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection, shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is South Coastal Regency
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of South Coastal.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of South Coastal Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus Organization hereinafter abbreviated as OPD is the Regional Apparatus Working Unit of the South Coastal Regency Regional Government.
6. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and increase of women's participation in development.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence which include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and in the state.
9. Protection of women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination.
11. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies.
12. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children.
13. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
14. Focal Point for Gender Mainstreaming is a Regional Apparatus Organization official who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
15. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically.
16. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect.
17. Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
19. Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in playing roles and participating in all fields.
20. Gender Justice is fair treatment of women and men, so that the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different.
21. Service is action that must be immediately taken to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
22. Safe House is temporary housing used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
23. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
27. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights.
28. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an institution established by the regional government to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

Article 31
(1) Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 28 paragraph (2) letter c aims for psychological recovery.
(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion or belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).
(3) Spiritual guidance is conducted by spiritual guidance officers.

Article 30
(1) Regional Government may provide safe houses for women and children who experience criminal and/or civil problems.
(2) The provision of safe house services aims to protect women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems who require a safe house include:
 a. their life is threatened;
 b. receiving rejection from family or community;
 c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
 d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

Article 32
(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) letter f constitute actions by law enforcement apparatus to implement laws and regulations in order to handle criminal and/or civil issues concerning women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.
(3) Types of legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
 a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
 b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
 c. legal assistance in the examination process at court;
 d. legal assistance in the court hearing decision process until a final legal decision is reached; and
 e. legal assistance in the mediation process.
(4) The Regional Government shall provide legal assistance to women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil issues based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(5) In providing legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3), UPTD PPA may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.

Article 26
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, victims' families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to complaint services submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 25 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of violence against women and children obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 33
(1) Repatriation is intended to return women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems to their place of origin.
(2) Repatriation of women and children as victims of criminal and/or civil problems is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

CHAPTER VII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 67
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Regional Government guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards, by facilitating the formulation of policies and regulations that serve as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection.
b. technical guidance and training, including:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement regarding the prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists, and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each OPD for the preparation of activity programs based on gender-responsive planning and budgeting.
c. Provision of facilities: the Regional Government provides facilities, means, and infrastructure in implementing women’s empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the formation of nagari that care for women and children;
e. Provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children.
(3) Supervision conducted by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. Monitoring, in the form of:
1. OPD leaders, in accordance with their duties and functions, are obligated to submit reports on the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection programs to the Regent.
2. Reports as referred to are submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
b. Evaluation, conducted in the form of:
1. The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women’s empowerment and child protection periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
2. In conducting supervision and evaluation, the Regent may appoint an OPD in accordance with its duties and functions.
3. The results of supervision and evaluation constitute evaluation material for policies of women’s empowerment and child protection programs.
(4) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), in order to realize the objectives of Women’s Empowerment and Child Protection, shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 67
